text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Increasing traffic has boosted reported disturbance in aviation in Finland this year, but no alarming deterioration of air security, aviation authority says.

- Unlike their American colleagues, Finnish secretaries with wrist injuries cannot demand compensation from computer manufacturers since the problem is not classified as an occupational illness in Finland. @
- The female hormone estrogen prevents contraction of blood vessels and therefore protects women from heart and blood disease, a new dissertation shows.
KAUPPALEHTI

- State asset management company Arsenal -- which has eight billion markka of real estate assets -- sees a strong market in 1997. This year, Arsenal has sold property for 1.3 billion markka and expects the full-year figure to be 1.4 billion compared to 1.2 billion last year. @
- Speculation mounts over who will succeed national mediator Jorma Reini after he was suspended from office. Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers negotiator Seppo Riski seen top candidate.

- Listed Finnish company bosses don't support private investor lobby's calls for dividend payout of half profits. Some would accept smaller portions, for instance one-third is supported by Amer, Cultor, Huhtamaki, Instrumentarium, Tamfelt and WSOY. @
- Most mutual funds in Finland have beaten the HEX general index in the 12 months to end-November.
- Finland sees EU pact with the U.S. to remove tariffs on information technology as coup for the country in EU.
- Sports and leisure goods wholesalers expect trade in the sector to grow over 10 percent next year. @
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET

- Metals and mining group Outokumpu has resolved a dispute with a Finnish businessman who registered a Web domain in Outokumpu's name, saying it only had to donate 4,000 markka to charity after demands as high as two million markka.

- Belorussian decathlon athlete and twice world championship silver medalist Eduard Hamalainen hopes for Finnish citizenship so he could represent Finland, where he has lived for two years, at Olympic Games in Athens. @
AAMULEHTI
- Owning one's home is cheaper in the long run than renting, according a study by the office for consumer affairs.
DEMARI
- A committee of experts set up to report on the effects on EMU on the Finnish economy plans to remain impartial on the subject until report is ready. @
